en.headline: Privacy chief warns of fake e-visa sites after 16 cases
en.dek: The Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data said 16 enquiries or complaints about fraudulent electronic-visa websites were received in three months, with losses of a few hundred to more than HK$1,700 per case.
body: Privacy Commissioner Ada Chung Lai-ling said the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data had received 16 enquiries or complaint cases over the past three months involving suspected fake electronic-visa websites.

Most cases concerned tourist visas for the United States, the United Kingdom and Thailand. Victims typically found the sites via search engines, submitted personal data and paid application fees ranging from a few hundred to more than HK$1,700 before discovering no visa was issued.

Chung advised the public not to trust top search results automatically, to check that official sites contain “gov” in the address, and to apply only through links provided by the relevant consulates-general or the Hong Kong government. Six suspected sites have been referred to law-enforcement agencies.

zh.headline: 假電子簽證網站湧現 私隱署三個月接16宗
zh.dek: 私隱專員鍾麗玲表示過去三個月接獲16宗假冒電子簽證網站查詢或投訴，主要涉美、英、泰旅遊簽證，損失數百至一千七百多元，呼籲勿盡信搜尋引擎置頂結果。
body: 個人資料私隱專員鍾麗玲今日表示，私隱專員公署過去三個月共接獲16宗涉及懷疑假冒電子簽證網站的查詢或投訴個案。
個案主要與美國、英國及泰國等旅遊簽證有關。事主多數透過搜尋引擎找到網站，提交個人資料並繳付數百至一千七百多元費用後，才發現無法取得簽證。
鍾麗玲提醒市民搜尋引擎置頂結果未必是官方網站，應留意網址是否含有「gov」字眼，並建議經相關總領事館或政府網站提供的連結申請。已有六個懷疑網站轉介執法機構跟進。
